digest.en: Brazil's first-round vote is counting live while Russia strikes a Kyiv bridge during Friedrich Merz's visit. The US pulled B-1 bombers from Fairford after a suspected terror threat. Yemen's presidency declared a full military drive to retake Houthi territory.

articles.title: Brazil presidential election 2026: first-round live results
articles.summary: Brazil holds its first-round presidential election, pitting incumbent Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva against Flávio Bolsonaro. The former president's son runs while his father remains imprisoned for plotting a coup. Candidates need over 50 percent of the vote to win outright. Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva is standing against Flávio Bolsonaro in the first round of the presidential raceThe incumbent, Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, is up against Flávio Bolsonaro, the son of the former president Jair Bolsonaro, who is in prison for plotting a military coup.

articles.title: US removes B-1 bombers from UK's Fairford air base amid security concerns
articles.summary: The US Air Force withdrew all B-1 bombers from RAF Fairford in England. The move followed arrests of men suspected of plotting a terror attack on the base. Prime Minister Andy Burnham stated Britain had strong indications of Iranian involvement in the scheme. The planes' removal comes after several men were arrested on suspicion of a terror plot on the air base, with UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham saying that Britain had "strong indications" that Iran was involved in the suspected plot targeting the base.

articles.title: U.S. Air Force removes all bombers from British air base targeted by a suspected terror attack
articles.summary: US bombers were removed from RAF Fairford after a suspected terror plot targeting the facility. The base had been used to strike Iran. The withdrawal follows an investigation into the planned attack on the US-run military installation in England. The U. S. Air Force has brought home its bombers stationed at a U. S.-run military air base in England used to strike Iran following an investigation into a planned terror attack at the RAF Fairford base.

articles.title: Nationalist Parties, Dodik Dominate Bosnian Election Amid Low Turnout
articles.summary: Milorad Dodik declared victory for his party in Bosnia's Serbian-led entity. Nationalist parties also won seats in the country's complex electoral system. Turnout was low. The results are likely to sustain high tensions across Bosnia and the wider region. Milorad Dodik, the Russia-friendly former leader of Bosnia-Herzegovina's Serbian-led entity, declared victory for his party in the region, with nationalist forces also scoring wins in Bosnia's complex electoral system -- results likely to keep tensions high in the country and the region.

articles.title: US, China And Russia Race To Build Nuclear Reactors On The Moon: Report
articles.summary: The United States plans to deploy a nuclear reactor on the lunar surface by 2030. Russia and China are coordinating a separate joint initiative targeting 2036. These power sources would support permanent bases and heavy industrial operations in space. The proposals have triggered regulatory debates regarding radiation containment and debris management. No agency has yet finalized the specific reactor designs or safety protocols for these extraterrestrial installations.

articles.title: Yemen presidency announces military drive to retake all Houthi territory
articles.summary: Rashad al-Alimi announced military operations to retake all remaining Houthi-held territory in Yemen. The presidential council head stated the goal is to extend state authority across the entire national territory. The campaign aims to restore government control over the republic. I announce today the start of military operations to retake the remaining territories of the republic and extend the authority of the state and its institutions across the entire national territory, says Rashad al-Alimi, the head of Yemen's presidential council.

articles.title: How a film brought a UN report to life in Xochimilco
articles.summary: A documentary based on United Nations University research screened at COP30 and European film festivals. The film returned to Xochimilco, the Mexico City canals where it was shot. This journey highlighted the local impact of the climate data presented in the report. A documentary drawn from United Nations University research was screened at the COP30 climate conference and film festivals across Europe.

articles.title: Bosnian Elections Pitted Pro-Western Against Nationalist Forces
articles.summary: Bosnian citizens voted on October 4 in elections for various political bodies. The contest pits pro-Western candidates against nationalist forces. Some candidates are pushing for faster integration into the European Union and NATO. Citizens in Bosnia-Herzegovina are casting their votes in elections to various bodies in the country’s multi-layered political system on October 4, with some candidates pushing for increased efforts at joining the European Union and NATO.

articles.title: Families Torn Apart, Trade At A Standstill: One Year Of The Afghan-Pakistan Border Closure
articles.summary: The Afghan-Pakistan border closure has lasted one year, halting cross-border trade. Tens of thousands of workers on both sides have lost their jobs. The shutdown has also disrupted commercial activity and strained family ties across the border. The prolonged closure of the Afghanistan-Pakistan border has brought cross-border trade to a standstill, leaving tens of thousands of people on both sides without work.

articles.title: US Coast Guard finds debris of missing air ambulance off coast of Massachusetts
articles.summary: The US Coast Guard is searching for a missing air ambulance jet that lost contact with the Federal Aviation Administration early Saturday. The aircraft was conducting a medical evacuation from Bermuda to Boston with six people onboard. The FAA issued a search and rescue alert after the plane failed to check in. Search operations are currently underway off the coast of Massachusetts.

articles.title: Russia Strikes Kyiv Bridge As Merz Visits Ukrainian Capital
articles.summary: Russia warned foreign diplomats to leave Ukraine or face mortal danger as it vowed to escalate air strikes on Kyiv. President Zelenskyy stated Ukraine will respond to the intensified Kremlin campaign. The threat targets non-citizens currently in the country. Russia has vowed to intensify its relentless strikes against Kyiv and warned foreign diplomats and other visitors to leave the country or be exposed to “mortal danger,” while Ukraine's leader said his country will respond to the Kremlin's deadly air campaign.

articles.title: US Lawmakers Target Serbia's Democratic Backsliding, Ties To Russia, China, Iran
articles.summary: A bipartisan group of US lawmakers is demanding stricter measures against Serbia. They cite democratic backsliding, corruption, and expanding Russian, Chinese, and Iranian influence. The pressure arrives just weeks before snap parliamentary elections. A bipartisan, bicameral group of US lawmakers is pressing for tougher action on what they describe as democratic backsliding, corruption, and growing Russian, Chinese, and Iranian influence in Serbia, just weeks before snap parliamentary elections.

articles.title: Ruined And Flooded, Russian-Occupied Oleshky In Ukraine Starves Under A 'Total Blockade'
articles.summary: Residents of Russian-occupied Oleshky in Ukraine's Kherson region face starvation. Land mines and supply cutoffs have created a total blockade. Ukrainian officials describe the area as a starving ghost town. People in Russian-held Oleshky in Ukraine's Kherson region have endured war, occupation, and devastating flooding. Now, trapped by land mines and cut off from basic supplies, they face "hell," starving in a virtual ghost town, Ukrainian officials and volunteers say.

articles.title: Flydubai attack feeds Netanyahu’s ‘protector’ line as polls near
articles.summary: A Flydubai flight carrying 170 passengers faced an attempted hijacking. The pilot and passengers prevented a major disaster. Netanyahu released a video warning of threats shortly before the incident. The event reinforces his narrative of constant security risks for Israel. The apparent attempted hijacking of a Flydubai flight carrying 170 mostly Israeli passengers was another reminder to Israelis of the constant threat of terror and war.

articles.title: New F-16s buy Taiwan time and space against China’s air coercion
articles.summary: Taiwan received its first two F-16V Block 70 jets at Chihhang Air Base. The aircraft provide breathing room against Chinese gray-zone coercion. However, increasing Chinese stealth capabilities limit their wartime utility. The delivery marks a significant step in Taiwan's air defense strategy. Taiwan’s new American-made F-16V Block 70 jets deliver much-needed breathing room against daily Chinese gray-zone coercion, yet surging Chinese stealth numbers and cratered runway risks mean their wartime utility would be sharply contested.

articles.title: Bangkok at breaking point as floods turn streets into stagnant lakes
articles.summary: Bangkok declared a disaster across all 50 districts after severe flooding. Forty people died as streets turned into stagnant lakes. Experts warn extreme flooding will worsen across south-east Asia. The city struggles to absorb sudden downpours during the rainy season. With 40 dead and a disaster declared across all 50 city districts, experts warn extreme flooding will only worsen across south-east AsiaBangkok is used to absorbing the sudden afternoon downpours that inundate the city during the rainy season.

articles.title: Flydubai Passenger Recounts Saving Stabbed Pilot
articles.summary: A Georgian-Israeli dentist on a Flydubai flight from Dubai to Israel helped a pilot allegedly stabbed by his co-pilot on September 30. Shota Musayev left his wife to assist the injured crew member. He feared for his own survival during the incident. The flight was diverted to safety. Georgian-Israeli dentist Shota Musayev told RFE/RL that he feared he might not survive when he left his wife’s side to help after the lead pilot was allegedly stabbed by his co-pilot during a Flydubai flight from Dubai to Israel on September 30.

articles.title: WHO appeals for massive aid influx ahead of winter
articles.summary: The World Health Organization warned that delayed medical supplies to Gaza risk devastating consequences. Lifesaving medicines and prosthetics are stuck in transit from Israel. The UN agency appealed for a massive aid influx before winter arrives. Palestinians in the enclave urgently need these critical resources. Repeated delays in bringing lifesaving medicines, prosthetics and more from Israel into Gaza risk having devastating consequences on Palestinians who urgently need them in the war-torn enclave, the UN World Health Organization (WHO) said on Friday.

articles.summary: Cairo authorities removed a 66-metre mural from Tahrir Square before Xi Jinping’s state visit. The artwork depicted Tutankhamun and Nefertiti with dark skin. articles.summary: Russian security forces detained fraud analyst Aleksandr Kynev in Moscow after he warned of vote falsifications benefiting United Russia. He was reportedly beaten while in custody. In the days between the elections and his arrest, Aleksandr Kynev had pointed to evidence of falsifications benefitting the United Russia party.

articles.title: US blast simulation targets China’s alleged secret nuke testing
articles.summary: The US Department of Energy conducted underground blast experiments in Nevada. These tests aim to detect clandestine nuclear detonations. The program addresses concerns about China's secret testing capabilities. Faced with rising great-power suspicions and the challenge of verifying clandestine, cavity-muffled detonations, the US is turning to high-precision subterranean blast experiments in the Nevada desert to strip covert nuclear testing of its technical cover.

articles.summary: Estonian slackliner Jaan Roose completed a 160-metre walk 120 metres above central Seoul on Thursday. articles.summary: The Trump administration redirected over $175 million from the state department human rights fund. This includes a $40 million grant for an anti-communism fund. articles.title: South African leader urges men to speak up on gender-based violence after series of killings
articles.summary: South African President Cyril Ramaphosa urged men to take greater responsibility for stopping gender-based violence. Cyril Ramaphosa acknowledged that not enough had been done to protect women.

hi.title: होर्मुज में जहाज पर फिर हमला, इंजन रूम तबाह, ईरान ने रास्ता खोलने के लिए रखीं 7 शर्तें
hi.summary: रविवार को होर्मुज स्ट्रेट में टैंकर पर हमले से इंजन रूम तबाह हो गया। ब्रिटेन की समुद्री एजेंसी UKMTO ने बताया कि क्रू सुरक्षित है। ईरान ने कहा कि अमेरिका के साथ जून के अंतरिम समझौते की सात शर्तें पूरी होने तक स्ट्रेट खुलेगा नहीं। होर्मुज स्ट्रेट में रविवार को एक टैंकर पर हमला हुआ है, जिससे उसके इंजन रूम को नुकसान पहुंचा.

articles.title: 'आप कैप्टन स्मित के देश से हैं', इजरायल में भारतीयों का बढ़ा रुतबा, क्या कह रहे इजरायली?
articles.summary: फ्लाईदुबई के कैप्टन स्मित मच्छर की बहादुरी के बाद इजरायल में भारतीय पर्यटकों को खास सम्मान मिल रहा है। तेल अवीव और यरुशलम में स्थानीय लोग भारतीयों से कहते हैं कि वे कैप्टन स्मित के देश से हैं। इस घटना ने भारतीयों के प्रति प्यार और अपनापन बढ़ाया है। फ्लाईदुबई की फ्लाइट में भारतीय कैप्टन स्मित मच्छर की बहादुरी के बाद इजरायल में भारतीय पर्यटकों को खास सम्मान मिल रहा है.
